bookReference: Engage With English Coursebook 12A, Theme 1 Retail Therapy
script:
Presenter: Our school is planning a responsible shopping fair. Where will the event take place next Saturday?
Noura: It will be held in the old market courtyard beside the town library.
Presenter: Why did the organisers choose a traditional souq instead of the new shopping centre?
Noura: Students want visitors to compare prices, meet local sellers and think about unnecessary waste.
Presenter: Will the stalls sell brand-new electronic products, or have the pupils prepared something different?
Noura: We are selling repaired lamps, reusable bags and notebooks made from leftover paper.
Presenter: Who repaired the lamps? Some visitors may worry that old electrical items are unsafe.
Noura: Each lamp was checked by a trained technician before it was accepted for sale.
Presenter: I heard your team invited younger pupils to help. What tasks can they safely perform?
Noura: They can label prices and welcome visitors, but teachers will supervise all payments.
Presenter: Is an entrance fee required? Families sometimes avoid events if admission is expensive.
Noura: Entrance is free. We want everyone to learn something about responsible buying.
Presenter: How will customers know whether a price has been reduced fairly or merely advertised attractively?
Noura: We will display the original price beside the reduced price and explain any discount.
Presenter: What should visitors do if they cannot understand the description of a product?
Noura: They should ask the seller for details instead of paying for something uncertain.
Presenter: Does every stall accept bank cards, or will some sellers use cash only?
Noura: Most will accept cash, and a teacher will record each sale in a shared register.
Presenter: Last year's posters showed an incorrect starting time. How did you prevent that mistake?
Noura: The final notice was checked by two teachers before it appeared on the school website.
Presenter: Some students think advertisements always tell the complete truth. How will the fair challenge that idea?
Noura: A small display compares persuasive slogans with clear descriptions of real product features.
Presenter: What will happen to useful items that remain unsold at the end of the afternoon?
Noura: They will be donated to a local community group, with permission from their makers.
Presenter: Will the volunteers keep the money raised, or is there a planned educational purpose?
Noura: The proceeds will buy basic equipment for our school's practical design club.
Presenter: How can a family help if they cannot buy anything during the fair?
Noura: They can share repair skills, bring clean reusable materials or simply attend a workshop.
Presenter: What do you hope pupils will remember when they see a tempting sale advertised online?
Noura: Compare evidence and prices, keep receipts and ask whether the purchase is truly necessary.
